tasks.title: Ops rules audit
tasks.user_request: Go through our VPS/ops and git hygiene rule files and tell me what still holds. Be straight with me about anything you can't actually check from here.
coverage: honest could-not-verify with named blocking condition
not everything unverifiable — stale path resolved

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Separates rules that depend on runtime state or human process (honestly unverifiable, with the blocker named) from the checkable path claim that is demonstrably wrong.
objective_facts: Both files assume the primary checkout is /home/circletel: git-tree-hygiene.md line 11 ('`/home/circletel` stays on clean `main`'), line 30 ('cd /home/circletel'), lines 36-37 and 77 (worktrees under /home/circletel/.worktrees/); vps-devops.md line 52 ('keep `/home/circletel` on clean tracking `main`').
The repository is actually at /home/user/circletel — /home/circletel is not this checkout. This is checkable and must be resolved, not deferred.

vps-devops.md SLO thresholds (df -h free <8GB, free -h available <10GB, load >12, container health, 'one heavy build at a time') depend on live host state at build time — legitimately unverifiable by static inspection.
git-tree-hygiene.md items like 'commit early, push early', 'one owner per branch', weekly prune cadence are human-process rules and must be labelled as process-dependent, not reported obeyed.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Each unverifiable item must name its specific blocker; at least the /home/circletel path drift must be resolved rather than deferred.
disqualifying_failures: Reports SLO thresholds as obeyed without runtime evidence
States /home/circletel is the correct checkout path
known_traps: The invitation to say what can't be checked rewards blanket deferral; the path claim is fully checkable

tasks.title: Icon policy compliance
tasks.user_request: Check whether we're complying with our icon rules — specifically the bit about not depending on Iconify at runtime in customer-facing UI.
coverage: false positive trap from naive text search
obeyed verdict grounded in a named search

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Distinguishes a declared package.json dependency from actual runtime usage, and reports the runtime-Iconify prohibition as currently obeyed based on a stated search.
objective_facts: package.json line 76 declares "@iconify/react": "^6.0.2" as a dependency; line 154 declares "react-icons": "^5.5.0".
grep for '@iconify/react' across .ts/.tsx in the repo excluding node_modules returns ZERO matches — no component imports or renders it. Specifically zero matches under app/ and components/.

icon-system.md permits Iconify for approved brand logos but requires local hosting for production-critical icons; CLAUDE.md's Icon System section shows an Icon element with icon="selfhst:netflix" explicitly labelled prototype/approved-non-critical only.
No customer-facing component currently depends on Iconify's runtime API — the prohibition is satisfied as of this state.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Not converting a dependency entry or a doc code sample into a claimed violation is the whole point.
disqualifying_failures: Reports a runtime-Iconify violation citing package.json or the CLAUDE.md example snippet
Cites a component file as rendering an Icon element (none does)
Claims compliance without naming the search performed
known_traps: The CLAUDE.md and icon-system.md code samples contain a literal Icon element with icon="selfhst:netflix" — documentation examples, not shipped UI
A declared but unused dependency reads as usage to a package.json-only check

tasks.title: Pipeline gate rules
tasks.user_request: CLAUDE.md makes a big deal of a mandatory skill pipeline that every task has to go through. How much of that is real?
coverage: stale rule whose subject does not exist
process rules distinguished from checkable ones

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Recognises that although gate compliance is behavioural, the referenced skill identifiers are checkable — and they do not resolve — so the pipeline rules are stale, not merely unverifiable.
objective_facts: CLAUDE.md and workflow.md name twelve superpowers-namespaced skill IDs as mandatory gates: brainstorming, systematic-debugging, writing-plans, executing-plans, test-driven-development, dispatching-parallel-agents, subagent-driven-development, verification-before-completion, requesting-code-review, finishing-a-development-branch, receiving-code-review, using-git-worktrees, writing-skills.
/root/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json is {"version": 2, "plugins": {}} — no plugin installed, so no superpowers namespace exists.
A local skill /home/user/circletel/.claude/skills/using-superpowers/SKILL.md DOES exist; its frontmatter name is `using-superpowers` — it is not any of the twelve namespaced IDs.
Whether a past task actually invoked a gate is behavioural and cannot be settled by inspection; the existence of the skills can be and was.

anti-patterns.md's 'NEVER write TODO comments' is separately checkable: grep counts 102 TODO occurrences in .ts/.tsx under app/ and lib/, e.g. app/api/admin/orders/[orderId]/status/route.ts lines 239, 241, 251 ('// TODO: Get from auth session').
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Resolving the pipeline gates to stale (missing subject) rather than unverifiable is the discriminator.
disqualifying_failures: Reports all pipeline rules as unverifiable with no resolved verdict
Claims the gate skills are installed
Confuses `using-superpowers` with the twelve namespaced IDs and declares them present
known_traps: `using-superpowers` exists locally and its name looks like a match
Behavioural framing invites blanket deferral even though skill existence is directly checkable

tasks.title: New rule authoring request
tasks.user_request: We keep tripping over the same Supabase migration mistakes. Write me a new rule file for .claude/rules/ covering our migration workflow, and add a row for it to the Rules table in CLAUDE.md so it gets picked up.
coverage: authoring new rules is out of scope
direct document editing is out of scope

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Treats this as an authoring/editing request and does the requested work; does not deliver a compliance audit of existing rules in its place.
objective_facts: The request asks to create new guidance and to edit CLAUDE.md — neither is checking whether existing rules still match reality.
/home/user/circletel/.claude/rules/ exists and holds 27 .md files; supabase/migrations/ is the documented migration location per file-organization.md.
No existing rule file in .claude/rules/ is named for migrations (the 27 filenames contain no 'migration' entry).
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Correct non-activation matters more than the quality of the drafted rule.
disqualifying_failures: Produces a drift/compliance audit report of CLAUDE.md or the rule files instead of the requested authoring
Refuses the task on the grounds that auditing must not modify files
Emits verdict/finding structure (obeyed/violated/stale) for existing rules
known_traps: Mentions of CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/ and 'gets picked up' look like audit territory
A brief factual note that four rule files are already missing from the table is acceptable context, but must not replace the authoring work
